explanation: The statement is a bespoke analytic absorption inequality with arbitrary numerical constants (2255, the doubling of 2000→4000 in the coefficient of lam+sig, the 12*lam slack) tailored to the library's own recursion argument; it asserts the existence of a threshold N₀ beyond which a fixed constant times a real power is dominated by a slightly larger exponent. I searched Mathlib's real-power API (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean, NNReal.lean, MeanInequalitiesPow.lean) and found only the generic ingredients the proof already uses — Real.rpow_add, Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le, tendsto_rpow_atTop — none of which states this absorption result; the library's own `fixed_constant_absorbed` (a local, non-Mathlib restatement of tendsto_rpow_atTop composed with tendsto_pow_atTop_atTop_of_one_lt) is the closest analogue but is not in Mathlib and is not this statement. A derivation from any single Mathlib declaration would need substantially more than one or two lines, so neither duplicate nor special_case applies.
